text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- (U.S. President) Clinton invites (Egyptian President) Mubarak, (Jordan's King) Hussein, (Palestinian President) Arafat and (Israeli Prime Minister) Netanyahu to an urgent meeting in Washington to discuss the crisis between Israel and Palestine. The White House: Mubarak is still considering whether or not to attend the meeting. Clinton, Hussein, Weizman and Christopher phone Mubarak and Arafat vists Cairo today.
- Israel is secretly digging another tunnel underneath the Tomb of the Patriarch in Hebron, Al-Ahram says.
- Netanyahu says that he would be pleased if Mubarak attended the summit.
- Israel's Labour party calls for a re-election.
- U.N. Security Council demands Israel end actions that have caused the crisis.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri tours Sharkiya governorate, inaugurates projects worth 120 million pounds.
- Clinton calls for a five-way summit in Washington Tuesday. Tension still grips the Palestinian territories.
- Ganzouri in Sharkiya: we are making all efforts to raise the standard of living of the people. The reform plan includes 75 billion pounds worth of investment annually.
- Two new oil and gas discoveries in Fayoum and Port Said

- Mubarak to Editor-in-Chief Samir Ragab: the only solution is fulfilling all agreements. I have warned and warned again that said and said again that things do not get solved by stones. If things are quiet now then who will guarantee that it will continue tomorrow.
